Ruling: class-one self-adjudication · letter C1 · authority ADR-0079 D3 (objectstack `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md`: 「`titleFormat` is deprecated … an explicit `nameField` takes precedence over it」) + the protocol text itself (`@objectstack/spec` `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:2122`, `titleFormat` describe: 「an explicit nameField now takes precedence」) + standing rule 「以协议为准:消费面对齐协议」 · 2026-09-14T00:36Z

## Ruling recorded — C1: `PageHeaderRenderer` aligns to the protocol — the declared pointer (`nameField` / `displayNameField`) outranks `titleFormat` in the header exactly as it does in `getRecordDisplayName`; the pin `titleFormat still outranks nameField` is rewritten to assert the opposite (director seat class-one adjudication, 2026-09-14)

Class-one self-adjudication by the summoned director seat, recorded for the maintainer's 追认表; an overturned row executes the new ruling.

**① Authority — protocol first, read on objectstack `origin/main` @ `57343f76`.** The contract both implementations claim to implement states the precedence in its own describe string — `titleFormat`: 「[DEPRECATED → nameField (ADR-0079)] Render-only title template; the server cannot return or query it, and **an explicit nameField now takes precedence**」. ADR-0079 D3 says the same in prose. `@object-ui/core`'s `getRecordDisplayName` (`packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts:28-34`) implements it (steps 1–2 declared pointer, step 3 LEGACY template). `PageHeaderRenderer`'s `resolvedTitle` ladder (`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:2054`, read on objectui `origin/main` @ `55f39ee9`) is the one consumer ranking the template above the resolver, and its own comment says it does so to 「mirror DetailView.resolveDisplayTitle」 — it copies another consumer, not the contract. Under 以协议为准 the consumer aligns to the protocol; this is not a choice between two equal orderings. C2 would amend an ADR to match one renderer; C3 keeps a green pin asserting the contract's negation.
**② Failure direction.** The change is visible at first render of any affected detail page (the H1 shows the declared title field) and the pin flips in the same PR — nothing silent; one revert restores the old ladder.
**③ Floors.** None moved: the ruling ENFORCES published contract semantics rather than changing them; no security boundary; no capability added or removed (`titleFormat` still renders as the fallback the contract already makes it); no gate weakened.

### What is ruled
1. In `PageHeaderRenderer`, the unified resolver (`getRecordDisplayName`) is consulted BEFORE the interpolated `titleFormat`; the template remains the fallback the contract assigns it — below the declared pointer, above bare record-key guesses.
2. `page-header-title.test.tsx` 「titleFormat still outranks nameField (legacy header behaviour)」 is retired and rewritten to pin the contract's ordering; a lit control keeps `titleFormat`-only objects rendering the template.
3. Mechanism assumption for the dev to verify, ⛔ not a ruling: the ladder's comment names `DetailView.resolveDisplayTitle` as what it mirrors — if that sibling still ranks the template above the declared pointer on today's tree, it is the same defect with the same fix and folds into this PR; if it already honours ADR-0079, say so in the report with the reading.
4. Acceptance note, ⛔ not a gate: the PR body records a census of first-party objects (examples, apps, hotcrm if reachable) declaring BOTH `nameField` and `titleFormat` — that count tells the maintainer whether this is a quiet correction or a visible rename; the letter does not depend on it.
5. The changeset declares the moved H1 output on a published renderer; level per AGENTS.md's changeset rules. The seat derives its own `Clause-②` line at claim (this pulls a consumer back to the declared contract and widens nothing) — ⛔ it does not inherit this sentence.
6. `page:header`'s own `schema.title` stays out of scope, as the card fences it.

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:ui` / `priority:p2` kept.
